messages:
morgan: noticed remote_write_queue_length for gpu-cluster up ~4x since 03:15, p95 remote_write latency at 2.6s, a bunch of timeouts :eyes:
leo: seeing same in prometheus sidecar metrics, sidecar logs show 'http2: stream reset' and intermittent 504s
triage-bot: rollout prom-sidecar-proxy v1.3.2 completed at 03:10, no crashloop events
nina: quick check — new pod annotation feature_x_id started appearing on all gpu pods after yesterday's infra rollout, could be exploding series cardinality
morgan: confirmed. series count (gpu_exporter) jumped 120k -> 1.2M around 03:12. prefix_kv cache pressure + bigger batches -> queue buildup. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/screens/ABCD1234
sre_oncall: can we drop that annotation at scrape-time? propose relabel in scrape_config to drop it temporarily
leo: +1. temporary relabel patch suggestion:
```
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_feature_x_id]
  action: drop
  regex: .+
```
leo: also for immediate mitigation bump remote_write timeout and queue capacity to give backpressure room:
```
remote_write:
  - url: https://rw-gpu.us-east1.redwood/internal
    timeout: 20s
    queue_config:
      capacity: 2500
      max_shards: 200
```
morgan: will apply relabel to prom-scrape-config configmap and canary to ap-sg first. deploying in 5m :thumbsup:
nina: heads up — sidecar logs also show a lot of TCP resets from natgw-ap-sg, port exhaustion is likely. NAT metrics show ephemeral_port_used ~ 0.98 of range
leo: that would explain stream resets even after relabel patch. if natgw is saturated, remote_write retries will pile up and create queue spikes
sre_oncall: we should schedule NAT port-range expansion + autoscale rule for natgw. quick fix: rotate some scrape traffic to us-west region (canary) — but that increases egress by ~+$1.2k/day, FYI
morgan: created INF-4321 to track natgw port-range + autoscale. tagging infra and networking. added cost note.
triage-bot: INF-4321 created and assigned to infra-team; priority: P2
leo: silenced alert PromRemoteWriteQueueHigh in ap-sg for 1h while we roll the relabel and observe
morgan: relabel patch applied to configmap and rolled to 3 scrapers in ap-sg (canary). early metrics: queue length down ~30% in canary nodes
nina: still seeing a handful of 504s but p95 remote_write latency down to 480ms in canary. NAT port backlog still present but reduced by rotating 10% traffic
morgan: will coordinate with infra for NAT fix in next low-traffic window. if all good we'll roll relabel cluster-wide in 30-60m
leo: follow-up: we should add an alert rule to detect sudden increase in unique label values on scrape target (cardinality delta) — simple PromQL: increase(count_values("label", metric)[5m]) > threshold
nina: agree. also add a per-scraper metric for annotation cardinality so we can alert before queue grows
morgan: can close this thread once cluster-wide relabel roll is done and natgw ticket scheduled
leo: noted. thanks everyone for quick triage :rocket:
nina: leaving a short runbook snippet here for oncall:
```
1) check prometheus_sidecar_queue_length{cluster="gpu"}
2) kubectl -n monitoring logs -l app=prom-sidecar | grep -i reset
3) inspect natgw ephemeral port usage in infra dashboard
4) apply relabel drop for pod annotation and canary the configmap
5) if natgw saturated, rotate traffic regionally and open INF ticket
```
morgan: canary roll finished, cluster-wide relabel applied at 03:42, queue levels stabilizing. closing for now, reopen if regressions.
